scenes.text: You are a tiny water droplet named Pip, resting in a calm lake on a sunny morning. The sun's warmth is growing stronger. What do you do?

choices.text: Rise into the air as water vapour
Sink deeper into the cool lake

scenes.text: You evaporate! Tiny and invisible, you float upward into the sky. This is called evaporation — it happens when liquid water turns into water vapour using energy from the sun. What do you do next?

choices.text: Keep rising higher into cooler air
Float sideways toward the mountains

scenes.text: The lake floor is cool and still. Plants nearby absorb some of the water through their roots — a process called absorption. Eventually, water that plants absorb is released through their leaves as vapour in a process called transpiration. You follow the journey upward.

choices.text: Evaporate through a leaf into the air
Stay underground and become groundwater

scenes.text: The air up here is cold! You and millions of other water vapour droplets bump together and condense around tiny dust particles, forming a cloud. Condensation is when water vapour cools and turns back into liquid. What does your cloud look like?

choices.text: A fluffy white cumulus cloud on a sunny day
A dark, heavy storm cloud full of rain

scenes.text: The mountains force the air higher. You cool rapidly and condense into a cloud above the peaks. From here, you can see the whole valley below. Snow glitters on the summit.

choices.text: Fall as rain on the mountain slope
Fall as snow on the summit

scenes.text: Underground, you travel slowly through rock and soil. This is called groundwater flow — it can take years! You eventually bubble up at a spring near a village and join a small stream.

choices.text: Flow along the stream to the ocean

scenes.text: Your fluffy cloud drifts over fields and forests for days. Farmers look up at you hopefully. Quiz time: what process formed you from water vapour?

choices.text: Evaporation
Condensation
Precipitation

scenes.text: Raindrops — including you — fall to the ground. This is precipitation. Water can also precipitate as snow, sleet, or hail depending on the temperature. You land on a hillside and begin to run downhill.

choices.text: Run off into a stream (surface runoff)
Soak into the soil (infiltration)

scenes.text: You are a snowflake! You settle on the mountain summit and become part of a glacier. Locked in ice, you might stay here for hundreds of years — until the climate warms and you melt, flowing down as glacial meltwater.

choices.text: Melt and flow down to the river

scenes.text: The river carries you past towns and farmland, getting wider and wider, until you reach the ocean. You are home again. The water cycle never ends — and neither does Pip's adventure!

choices.text: Rest in the ocean (you have completed the cycle!)

scenes.text: Not quite! Evaporation is when liquid water turns into vapour — that already happened to Pip at the lake. The cloud you see formed through condensation: the vapour cooled and turned back into tiny liquid droplets. Remember: condensation makes clouds!

choices.text: Continue the journey — fall as rain

scenes.text: Correct! Condensation is when water vapour cools and turns back into tiny liquid droplets that cluster together to form clouds. Well done, Pip!

choices.text: Continue the journey — fall as rain

scenes.text: Not yet — precipitation is the step when the cloud releases water as rain or snow. The cloud itself formed through condensation, when water vapour cooled into droplets. You are close — keep going!

choices.text: Continue the journey — fall as rain

scenes.text: Pip settles into the warm ocean, one droplet among trillions. Somewhere above, the sun is already warming the surface — and a new journey is about to begin. You have completed the water cycle!
